The claim states that the method differs from Variable-Length Coding because Variable-Length Coding 'assigns a fixed bit depth to an entire data block based on its local value range.' However, Source [S3] defines Huffman coding (a standard variable-length coding method) as assigning 'shorter codewords to more frequent symbols and longer codewords to less frequent symbols' based on symbol probability, not a fixed bit depth for a block. Furthermore, Source [S1] states that the method in question uses DEFLATE (which includes Huffman coding) and that 'entropy encoding reduces the two codebook indices to their required bit-length according to codebook sizes,' which implies variable-length coding based on frequency/probability, similar to the description of Huffman coding in [S3]. The claim's description of Variable-Length Coding is factually incorrect according to the provided evidence, and the distinction drawn is not supported by the texts.

The evidence supports the mechanism of tree traversal for decoding.
